sections.category: Anthropic's Claude reaches general availability inside Microsoft Foundry, running on Azure-hosted NVIDIA GB300 Blackwell Ultra

bullets.body: Anthropic and Microsoft moved Claude from preview to general availability inside Microsoft Foundry on June 29, giving Azure-native enterprises a first-party way to call Claude under the identity, networking, billing and governance controls they already run. The launch ships Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Haiku 4.5 through the Messages API with prompt caching and extended-thinking support, and offers two deployment shapes — "hosted on Azure," which runs end-to-end on Azure infrastructure and is the generally available tier, versus "hosted on Anthropic infrastructure," which stays in preview — plus a single consolidated Azure invoice and Microsoft Enterprise Agreement integration for eligible customers. The infrastructure story is the differentiator: the Azure-hosted tier runs on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems with Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking, with NVIDIA pitching the GB300's inference efficiency as a total-cost-of-ownership reducer and pairing the rollout with its Secure Agent Workspace reference design for building autonomous, domain-specific agents. The read-through is that the PaaS-LLM layer is consolidating: a frontier lab's flagship models now sit alongside the hyperscaler's own catalog on the hyperscaler's silicon, narrowing the gap between "use the lab's API" and "deploy inside your cloud tenant."

sections.category: vLLM ships v0.24.0 with a quantized-by-default Model Runner V2, multi-tier KV-cache offloading, and a maturing Rust frontend

bullets.body: The dominant open-source inference server cut a major release, vLLM v0.24.0, landing 571 commits from 256 contributors and pushing several pieces of the local-LLM serving stack forward at once. The engine-level changes are the substantive ones: Model Runner V2 now supports quantized models by default, a multi-tier KV-cache offloading path adds an object-store secondary tier for spilling cache beyond GPU memory, DeepSeek-V4 got another large optimization pass with a sparse index cache and prefill chunk-planning, and DeepEP v2 was integrated for expert parallelism on MoE models. On raw kernels, the release claims a 180-290% speedup for SM90 CUTLASS FP8 via a swap_ab optimization and adds native DSA indexer decode on SM100, while the Rust frontend matured with API authentication, CORS and tokenization endpoints plus a streaming parser that unifies tool-call and reasoning parsing. Launch-day model coverage tracks the current open-weight wave — MiniMax-M3 with AMD/ROCm optimizations, DiffusionGemma with CPU support, and unified FlashAttention for Gemma 4 — reinforcing that the serving layer, not just the models, is where a lot of the 2026 throughput-per-dollar gains are now being booked.

sections.category: New arxiv work proposes WorldEvolver: self-evolving world models that update at inference time to sharpen LLM-agent planning

bullets.body: A paper submitted to arXiv on June 29, "Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning" by Xuan Zhang, Wenxuan Zhang, See-Kiong Ng and Yang Deng, targets a concrete failure mode in agent harnesses: agents plan badly because they predict the consequences of their actions badly. The proposed framework, WorldEvolver, improves that action-outcome prediction through three coupled components — an episodic memory that recalls past interactions, a semantic memory that distills explicit rules from prediction errors, and a selective-foresight mechanism that filters out unreliable predictions before they reach the planner. The notable design choice is that the world model keeps evolving during deployment while the core agent stays frozen, so the system adapts at inference time without retraining the backbone. The authors report the highest prediction accuracy across three different backbone models and higher downstream task-success rates than competing world-model baselines on interactive environments, which positions runtime memory updates as a cheaper lever for agent reliability than full fine-tuning — relevant to the orchestration and coding-agent harnesses that increasingly depend on accurate forward simulation.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: AI Engineer World's Fair is mid-run in San Francisco, with summer and fall chip and security dates locked

bullets.body: The forward calendar across all three sub-tracks, refreshed as of June 30. Mainstream dev/data: the AI Engineer World's Fair is mid-run at Moscone West in San Francisco (June 29 through July 2; ~29 tracks, ~300 speakers, ~100 expo partners, 6,000+ attendees), with the Autoresearch keynote and ~12 parallel tracks on July 1 and the Harness Engineering keynote on July 2; further out, GitHub Universe returns October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas. AI-security: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay; Black Hat USA 2026 brings its AI Summit plus the main Briefings to Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas in early August, with DEF CON 34 and its AI Village the same week; OWASP Global AppSec USA is November 5-6 in San Francisco; and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series continues to additional cities after its San Francisco stop, so it stays on the watch list. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is July 22-23 at Moscone (Instinct MI400-series focus on July 23), Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford's Memorial Auditorium, and the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center. Treat this bullet as an attendance planner: the security and chip tracks are where the secure-AI-accelerator and agent-hijack threads from recent weeks will surface in person.
